A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SafeDiffCon and the same three control tasks. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, support comparison; relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: Sections 5.1–5.4 and Tables 1–4 report original simulation-based control evaluations and component ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds original timing measurements, further ablations and parameter sensitivity results in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The conformal weighting, diffusion losses, post-training and guided fine-tuning procedures remain unchanged, including Algorithms 1–3. DDIM sampling was already specified in v1 Tables 6–7; v2's efficiency discussion does not establish a new sampling procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use Burgers control, incompressible-fluid smoke routing and tokamak simulator control. The new analyses reuse these tasks. Internal inductance was already a stated tokamak control target in v1, so its insertion into the objective equation does not establish new task coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 retain the same comparator membership and baseline implementations. The new timing comparison uses BC, PID, SL-Lag, MPC-Lag, CDT and TREBI, all already evaluated on Burgers in v1.

E3.justification: V2 adds timing and parameter-sweep protocols while retaining the main splits, architectures and training budgets. The printed tokamak objective changes from beta_p error alone to beta_p plus l_i error, matching the existing prose; rerunning is not established. Tables 8–9 have conflicting captions and headers, leaving the precise parameter-to-value mapping uncertain.

E4.justification: V1's component ablations cover only the 2D fluid task. V2 adds corresponding removal experiments for Burgers and tokamak control in Tables 6–7, plus sensitivity analyses for coverage probability, training/calibration split and objective weight in Tables 8–10. This substantially broadens component validation and robustness analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run counts, error bars or significance tests. The conformal uncertainty construction is unchanged; varying its coverage parameter adds sensitivity experiments rather than a new statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 retain their numerical results. Tables 5–10 add substantial timing, ablation and sensitivity evidence: SafeDiffCon takes 2.3575 minutes versus TREBI's 13.5525, and tokamak ablations report 10%, 50% and 28% unsafe trajectories after removing post-training, fine-tuning and Q, respectively. These are newly reported results, not improved main benchmark scores.

T1.justification: The tokamak objective definition gains the squared internal-inductance error term in v2 Equations 18–19, absent from v1 Equation 18. This corrects the formula to match the stated two-target objective. Theorems 4.1–4.3 and the Appendix A proofs remain unchanged apart from numbering.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about safe PDE control, conformal adaptation and superior control performance subject to safety across the three tasks. The new appendix evidence does not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix B newly attributes inference efficiency to post-training and DDIM and interprets the parameter sweeps as showing robustness. That robustness claim is insufficiently qualified despite some settings producing 2–4% unsafe trajectories. The existing main-text interpretations and Section 6 limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix B.1 newly identifies an A800 with eight CPUs for the timing measurements and explains the existing DDIM choice. Other implementation and hyperparameter details are retained. The abstract repeats the repository URL already linked in v1 Section 5, so no new code availability is established.

R1.justification: V2 adds Song, Meng and Ermon's DDIM paper in Appendix B.1 and the references. The related-work discussion and novelty positioning otherwise remain unchanged; the Barros reference changes only bibliographic metadata.

P1.justification: V2 makes limited introductory edits, corrects residual SafeConPhy naming and the PID expansion, and updates affiliations and publication text. It inserts Appendix B and replaces acknowledgements with an Impact Statement. The main narrative and matched earlier appendices remain largely intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds compact Tables 5–10 alongside retained appendix visualizations, reduces Figure 4's size, moves algorithm displays and other floats, and corrects Figure 2's caption. All five figures retain their visual content, and existing table structures remain unchanged; the presentation changes are localized.

improvement.justification: The added timing and cross-task ablations address gaps in v1, and the tokamak formula now matches the stated targets. However, new Table 6 reports 4% unsafe trajectories alongside 50% unsafe timesteps, Tables 8–9 conflict on parameter labels, and Table 10 contradicts the defined negative objective. These unresolved inconsistencies undermine the added evidence, preventing a reliable judgment of net overall quality improvement.
